title: improv·artist · minimal (Lee Ufan)
mutation_directive: improv artist: minimal via Lee Ufan

improv_extras.practice: single brushstroke per canvas; mono-ha; stone and steel as encounter

v1.feedback: Strong execution of Lee Ufan's From Point logic — the paint-reload-every-12 diminishment is a genuine encoding of his technique, not decoration. The sumi-ink-on-cream palette and post-settling breath are exactly right. Two refinements: the stone feels undersized relative to the stamp field — in Relatum, the stone commands equal visual weight to the surrounding gesture; scale it up or shift camera to give it more presence. Second, the 7×7 grid reads as perfectly regular — Lee Ufan's grids have subtle hand-wobble in spacing that makes the human gesture legible; adding ±0.15 jitter to stamp centers would strengthen that reading.

v2.feedback: Strong concept translation — the 7×7 stamp grid with 12-touch ink depletion directly references Ufan's From Point method, and the stone encounter captures Relatum's 'ma' between gesture and matter. The stone's surface bump (sin-based deformation at 6%+4%) reads slightly too smooth for a mono-ha boulder; increase bump amplitude to ~12% with more frequency harmonics so the silhouette reads as rough granite rather than polished ellipsoid. Consider making the stamp opacity falloff more dramatic — the current 7.5%-per-touch linear depletion is subtle; Ufan's late stamps in a sequence are barely visible ghosts, so the last 3–4 stamps in each reload should approach near-transparency to sell the ink-exhaustion narrative.
